definition: The internal variables a model learns from data — weights and biases adjusted during training.
details: The internal variables a model learns from data — weights and biases adjusted during training. Parameter count is the standard rough measure of model capacity.

explainer.lead: Machine learning parameters are the internal variables a model learns from data—weights and biases adjusted during training. Parameter count is the standard rough measure of model capacity.

tiers.eli5: Think of the knobs inside a machine that get twisted during practice; the number of knobs gives a rough idea of how much the machine can handle.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers treat parameter count as a rough gauge of model capacity when choosing or comparing models. A pitfall is reading capacity from parameter count alone, since it is only a rough measure.
tiers.paperLevel: Parameters are the internal variables a model learns from data—weights and biases adjusted during training; parameter count is the standard rough measure of model capacity. Limit: the measure is rough, not a precise account of capability.

explainer.example: Comparing two models by their parameter counts gives a quick rough sense of which has more capacity before any training results are in.
